query: how to build an ai agent without code
title: How to build an AI agent without code in 7 steps | 50agents
description: How to build an AI agent without code: pick one job, write its instructions, connect only the apps it needs, test it on real cases, and approve every send.
h1: How to build an AI agent without code
answer: Pick one job that needs judgement, write it as a job card, and test it on 10 to 20 real cases.
Start it read-only, and let it draft rather than send until its drafts need no edits.

body.p: An AI agent is three parts: a model, the tools it can use, and its instructions. A no-code builder picks the model and turns the other two into forms. Your work is the instructions and the limits.

Check you need one first. If your job is "when X happens, do Y", fixed steps will do it cheaper and the same way every time: read [AI agent vs automation](/guides/ai-agent-vs-automation-which-one-you-need).

sections.h2: Write the job card before you open any tool

head: Line
Example: follow up quiet deals
rows: Draft follow-ups for deals gone quiet

body.p: The last line is the one people forget. With no instruction for the unclear case, an AI agent guesses, and a confident guess is the most common failure.

method.h2: How to build an AI agent in 7 steps

steps.title: Choose one job, not a role
steps.body: "Follow up quiet deals" is a job. "Be my sales assistant" is a role, and it will do a little of everything badly. Add a second AI agent later.

steps.title: Collect 10 to 20 real examples
steps.body: Real emails, deals or tickets, including two or three awkward ones. They are your test set; without them you are judging the AI agent on a demo.

steps.title: Connect only the apps it needs
steps.body: Give it read access first, on the narrowest account or folder the builder allows. See [how to give an AI agent access safely](/guides/how-to-give-an-ai-agent-access-to-your-apps-safely).

note.text: An AI agent connected to your admin account can do anything you can. Use a narrower account where the app has one.

steps.title: Paste in the job card as instructions
steps.body: Plain sentences: the case it handles, the output you want, and what to do when unsure. [How to write instructions for an AI agent](/guides/how-to-write-instructions-for-an-ai-agent) has a template.

steps.title: Run it on your examples by hand
steps.body: Read every result, fix the instructions where it went wrong, and run the set again. Stop when two runs in a row need no edits on most cases.

steps.title: Put sends behind an approval
steps.body: Anything that emails a customer, spends money or changes a record waits for your yes. Loosen this one action at a time, once you trust it.

steps.title: Schedule it and read its first week
steps.body: Turn on the schedule, then read each run's report for a week. Most problems show up in the first five runs.

note.text: Add every case it got wrong to your test set, and rerun the set each time you change the instructions.

captain.line: Tell Captain the job in one sentence: it writes the plan from your words, checks the apps are connected, and shows you the plan before it builds.

wrong.title: It does a bit of everything
wrong.body: The job was a role. Split it into one AI agent per job, each with its own schedule and apps.

wrong.title: Confident wrong answers
wrong.body: It filled a gap with a guess. Tell it what to do when unsure ("skip it and tell me why"), and give it the facts it lacks.

wrong.title: It works in the demo, not on Monday
wrong.body: You tested on clean examples. Add your awkward cases to the test set and run them after every change.

wrong.title: Costs climb
wrong.body: Each run reads more than it needs: whole inboxes, every deal. Narrow the search to the last 24 hours or open deals only.

wrong.title: An app silently stops working
wrong.body: A connection expired or a permission changed. Pick a builder that tells you when a run fails, and read failures the same day.

faqs.q: Can I build an AI agent for free?
faqs.a: Most builders have a free tier that covers testing, and 50agents is free to start. Run your AI agent on a few real cases before you schedule it daily.

faqs.q: How long does it take to build one?
faqs.a: Building takes minutes once the job card is written. Getting it right takes one or two rounds of testing on real examples, usually an afternoon.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?
faqs.a: A chatbot answers when you write to it. An AI agent has a job, a schedule or a trigger, and access to your apps, so it works while you are elsewhere and reports back.
